answers.explanation: Programs keep stopping to wait, and the CPU sits idle unless there's other work.
Switching to another ready job keeps the CPU busy.
Batch systems ran jobs one after another, keeping the hardware busy.
Job scheduling picks which job runs.
It keeps only a subset of the total jobs in memory.
2 ms of 10 ms is 20%. The other 80% is wasted without another job to run.
The OS sits in low memory; jobs share the rest.
